facts.text: Paris, Virginia, was named in 1819 to honor Marquis de Lafayette's 1814 tour of the United States after the War of 1812.
Paris Historic District, listed on the Virginia Landmarks Register in 2006 and the National Register in 2007, preserves 34 1810–1850 Federal‑style buildings.
When the Manassas Gap Railroad routed south in 1852, Paris was bypassed, preserving its architecture but causing commercial decline.
Before European arrival, the area that became Paris was part of the Manahoac Siouan‑speaking confederacy’s northern Piedmont territory.
The old Ashby Hotel tavern, once the town’s main street hub, was destroyed in 1939 by a runaway truck.
The original 1830 brick Old Meetinghouse served multiple denominations, later became an African‑American school, and now houses private residences.
